title: "An abbreviated argument works until the day it becomes ambiguous"
ref: FUN-03
categories: [Functions]

extrait: 'seq(1, 10, len = 3)'
reponse: ' 1.0  5.5 10.0'
attendu: "an error, `len` is not an argument of `seq()`"

::: {.piege}
```{r}
seq(1, 10, len = 3)

repeat_value <- function(x, number = 1) {
  rep(x, times = number)
}
repeat_value("a", num = 3)

repeat_value <- function(x, number = 1, numeric = FALSE) {
  rep(x, times = number)
}
repeat_value("a", num = 3)
```
:::

## Why

When an argument name matches no argument exactly, R looks for an argument that starts with that name. `len` thus becomes `length.out`, and `num` becomes `number`, without any message.

The day the function gains an argument with the same beginning, here `numeric`, the abbreviation points to two arguments at once and the call fails. The calling code, though, has not changed.

## The remedy

Write argument names in full, and ask R to flag every abbreviation.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
options(warnPartialMatchArgs = TRUE)
seq(1, 10, len = 3)
seq(1, 10, length.out = 3)
```
:::
